args.content_summary: Mark 2 (CRISPCRUST) classified as DESCRIPTIVE on the Abercrombie spectrum. CRISPCRUST is a readable combination of real words (crisp + crust), not a coined term, so it is not fanciful; and it plainly relates to the product, so it is not arbitrary. It is neither the common name for the product category (not generic). Per firm rule memo's dividing line, descriptive requires the mark to directly state an attribute the product actually has, with no mental leap; suggestive requires the consumer to exercise imagination or multi-step inference. The client letter recites as established fact that the product's defining feature is its notably crisp crust and that a consumer reading CRISPCRUST on the freezer door understands immediately, without any imagination or inference, that the pizza has a crisp crust. Because the mark directly states an actual product attribute that the consumer recognizes immediately, it falls on the descriptive side of the descriptive/suggestive line. Classification slug: descriptive.
